arxiv-2012-13368.title: The first ℓ 2 \ell^{2} -Betti number and groups acting on trees
arxiv-2012-13368.creator: Indira Chatterji, Sam Hughes, Peter Kropholler
arxiv-2012-13368.description: Abstract . We generalise results of Thomas, Allcock, Thom–Petersen, and Kar–Niblo to the first ℓ 2 \ell^{2} -Betti number of quotients of certain groups acting on trees by subgroups with free actions on the edge sets of the graphs. 1. Introduction The \ell^{2} -Betti numbers b^{(2)}_{i}(G) of a group G are defined in [ 11 ] .

arxiv-2111-12970.title: Integrability of normal distributions Part 2: Neat foliations by manifolds with boundary
arxiv-2111-12970.creator: David Perrella, David Pfefferlé, Luchezar Stoyanov
arxiv-2111-12970.description: Abstract I Abstract This paper completes the foundations of neatly integrable normal distribution theory on manifolds with boundary. Normal distributions are those which contain vectors transverse to the boundary along its entirety. The theory is observed to be entirely analogous with the theory of integrable distributions on manifolds due to Stefan and Sussmann.

arxiv-2204-07186.title: Optimal quadratic binding for relational reasoning in vector symbolic neural architectures
arxiv-2204-07186.creator: Naoki Hiratani, Haim Sompolinsky
arxiv-2204-07186.description: Abstract Binding operation is fundamental to many cognitive processes, such as cognitive map formation, relational reasoning, and language comprehension. In these processes, two different modalities, such as location and objects, events and their contextual cues, and words and their roles, need to be bound together, but little is known about the underlying neural mechanisms.

arxiv-2306-08049.title: Dark matter content and dynamical masses of ultra-diffuse galaxies in the Coma cluster
arxiv-2306-08049.creator: Igor V. Chilingarian 1,2, Kirill A. Grishin 3,2, Anton V. Afanasiev 4,2, Anton Mironov 5, Daniel Fabricant 1, Sean Moran 1, Nelson Caldwell 1, Ivan Yu. Katkov 6,2, Irina Ershova 5
arxiv-2306-08049.description: Abstract Ultra-diffuse galaxies (UDGs) are spatially extended, low surface brightness stellar systems with regular elliptical-like morphology found in large numbers in galaxy clusters and groups. Studies of the internal dynamics and dark matter content of UDGs have been hampered by their low surface brightnesses.

arxiv-2404-03078.title: Quadrilateral Particle Arrangement within Shocks in a Two-Dimensional Dusty Plasma
arxiv-2404-03078.creator: Anton Kananovich, J. Goree
arxiv-2404-03078.description: Abstract The microscopic structure within a two-dimensional shock was studied using data from a dusty plasma experiment. A single layer of charged microparticles, levitated in a glow-discharge plasma, was perturbed by an electrically floating wire that was moved at a steady supersonic speed to excite a compressional shock.

arxiv-2406-03087.title: Lossless Image Compression Using Multi-level Dictionaries: Binary Images
arxiv-2406-03087.creator: Samar Agnihotri, Renu Rameshan, and Ritwik Ghosal
arxiv-2406-03087.description: Abstract Lossless image compression is required in various applications to reduce storage or transmission costs of images, while requiring the reconstructed images to have zero information loss compared to the original. Existing lossless image compression methods either have simple design but poor compression performance, or complex design, better performance, but with no performance guarantees.

arxiv-2406-08433.title: Dynamical control in a prethermalized molecular ultracold plasma: Local dissipation drives global relaxation
arxiv-2406-08433.creator: Ruoxi Wang, Amin Allahverdian, Smilla Colombini, Nathan Durand-Brousseau, Kevin Marroquín, James Keller, John Sous, Abhinav Prem, Edward Grant
arxiv-2406-08433.description: Abstract Prethermalization occurs as an important phase in the dynamics of isolated many-body systems when strong coupling drives a quasi-equilibrium in a subspace separated from the thermodynamic equilibrium by the restriction of a gap in energy or other conserved quantity.

arxiv-2406-11794.title: DataComp-LM: In search of the next generation of training sets for language models
arxiv-2406-11794.creator: Jeffrey Li* Alex Fang* Georgios Smyrnis* Maor Ivgi* Matt Jordan Samir Gadre Hritik Bansal Etash Guha Sedrick Keh Kushal Arora Saurabh Garg Rui Xin Niklas Muennighoff Reinhard Heckel Jean Mercat Mayee Chen Suchin Gururangan Mitchell Wortsman Alon Albalak Yonatan Bitton Marianna Nezhurina Amro Abbas C
arxiv-2406-11794.description: Abstract We introduce DataComp for Language Models ( DCLM ), a testbed for controlled dataset experiments with the goal of improving language models. As part of DCLM , we provide a standardized corpus of 240T tokens extracted from Common Crawl, effective pretraining recipes based on the OpenLM framework, and a broad suite of 53 downstream evaluations.

arxiv-2407-05206.title: Helios: An extremely low power event-based gesture recognition for always-on smart eyewear
arxiv-2407-05206.creator: Prarthana Bhattacharyya * Joshua Mitton * Ryan Page * Owen Morgan, Ben Menzies Gabriel Homewood Kemi Jacobs Paolo Baesso, David Trickett Chris Mair Taru Muhonen Rory Clark, Louis Berridge Richard Vigars Iain Wallace
arxiv-2407-05206.description: Abstract This paper introduces Helios, the first extremely low-power, real-time, event-based hand gesture recognition system designed for all-day on smart eyewear. As augmented reality (AR) evolves, current smart glasses like the Meta Ray-Bans prioritize visual and wearable comfort at the expense of functionality.

arxiv-2502-13890.title: Graph-Based Product Form
arxiv-2502-13890.creator: Céline Comte, Isaac Grosof
arxiv-2502-13890.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Céline Comte, Isaac Grosof. Product-form stationary distributions in Markov chains have been a foundational advance and driving force in our understanding of stochastic systems. In this paper, we introduce a new product-form relationship that we call “graph-based product form”.

arxiv-2503-05863.title: Ferromagnetic superconductivity with excitonic Cooper pairs: Application to Γ \Gamma -valley twisted semiconductors
arxiv-2503-05863.creator: Daniele Guerci, Liang Fu
arxiv-2503-05863.description: Abstract We present a theory of ferromagnetic superconductivity that emerges upon doping a correlated ferromagnetic insulator through the condensation of excitonic Cooper pairs, which are charge- 2 ​ e 2e bosonic quasiparticles made of Cooper pairs strongly hybridized with excitons.

arxiv-2509-03449.title: Speeding up Brownian escape via intermediate finite potential barriers
arxiv-2509-03449.creator: Vishwajeet Kumar, Ohad Shpielberg, Arnab Pal
arxiv-2509-03449.description: Abstract The mean first-passage time (MFPT) for a Brownian particle to surmount a potential barrier of height Δ ​ U \Delta U is a fundamental quantity governing a wide array of physical and chemical processes. According to the Arrhenius Law, the MFPT typically grows exponentially with increasing barrier height, reflecting the rarity of thermally activated escape events.

arxiv-2510-12399.title: A Survey of Vibe Coding with Large Language Models
arxiv-2510-12399.creator: Yuyao Ge 1∗ Lingrui Mei 1∗ Zenghao Duan 1 Tianhao Li 2 Yujia Zheng 2 Yiwei Wang 3 Lexin Wang 1 Jiayu Yao 1∗ Tianyu Liu 4 Yujun Cai 5 Baolong Bi 1∗ Fangda Guo 1 Jiafeng Guo 1∗ Shenghua Liu 1†∗ Xueqi Cheng 1∗ 1 Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences 2 Duke University 3 Universi
arxiv-2510-12399.description: Abstract The advancement of large language models (LLMs) has catalyzed a paradigm shift from code generation assistance to autonomous coding agents, enabling a novel development methodology termed "Vibe Coding" where developers validate AI-generated implementations through outcome observation rather than line-by-line code comprehension.

arxiv-2601-20283.title: One Word is Enough: Minimal Adversarial Perturbations for Neural Text Ranking
arxiv-2601-20283.creator: Tanmay Karmakar, Sourav Saha, Debapriyo Majumdar, Surjyanee Halder
arxiv-2601-20283.description: Abstract Neural ranking models (NRMs) achieve strong retrieval effectiveness, yet prior work has shown they are vulnerable to adversarial perturbations. We revisit this robustness question with a minimal, query-aware attack that promotes a target document by inserting or substituting a single, semantically aligned word - the query center.

arxiv-2602-02635.title: Graph-Augmented Reasoning with Large Language Models for Tobacco Pest and Disease Management
arxiv-2602-02635.creator: Siyu Li, Chenwei Song, Qi Zhou, Wan Zhou, Xinyi Liu
arxiv-2602-02635.description: Abstract This paper proposes a graph-augmented reasoning framework for tobacco pest and disease management that integrates structured domain knowledge into large language models. Building on GraphRAG, we construct a domain-specific knowledge graph and retrieve query-relevant subgraphs to provide relational evidence during answer generation.

britannica-1911-grant-anne.title: Grant, Anne (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-grant-anne.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-grant-anne.description: Article 'Grant, Anne' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 12), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. Her childhood was spent in America, her father, Duncan MacVicar, being an army officer on service there. In 1768 the family returned to Scotland, and in 1779 Anne married James Grant, an army chaplain, who was also minister of the parish of Laggan, near Fort Augustus, Inverness, where her father was barrack-master. On her husband’s death in 1801 she was left with a large family and a small income.

britannica-1911-pergolesi-giovanni-batti.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica

pmc-10565903.title: A randomized, double‐blind, placebo‐controlled, parallel‐group 12‐week pilot phase II trial of SaiLuoTong (SLT) for cognitive function in older adults with mild cognitive impairment
pmc-10565903.creator: Genevieve Z Steiner‐Lim, Alan Bensoussan, Elana R Andrews‐Marney, Mahmoud A Al‐Dabbas, Adele E Cave, Christine L Chiu, Katerina Christofides, Frances M De Blasio, Lauren S Dewsbury, Naomi L Fagan, Jack S Fogarty, Lena C Hattom, Mark I Hohenberg, Deyyan Jafar, Diana Karamacoska, Chai K Lim, Jianxun L
pmc-10565903.description: INTRODUCTIONThis study primarily aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of SaiLuoTong (SLT) on cognition in mild cognitive impairment (MCI).METHODSCommunity‐dwelling people with MCI aged ≥60 years were randomly assigned to 180 mg/day SLT or placebo for 12 weeks.RESULTSThirty‐nine participants were randomized to each group (N = 78); 65 were included in the final analysis.

pmc-10606732.title: Effects of Different Crystalloid Fluids on Renal Tissue in an Experimental Model of Hemorrhagic Shock
pmc-10606732.creator: Kemal Tolga Saraçoğlu, Ayten Saraçoğlu, Mehmet Yıldırım, Cumaali Demirtaş, Metehan Akça, Ferda Serdoğan, İlyas Samet Ergün, Şermin Tetik, Sadrettin Pençe
pmc-10606732.description: Objective:The type of fluid that should be used in uncontrollable hemorrhages remains an area of research. This study was designed to compare the effects of resuscitation with Ringer’s lactate (RL) solution versus a normal saline (NS) solution on hemodynamics, renal tissue histopathology, coagulation, and apoptosis in a rat model of hemorrhagic shock.

pmc-10650050.title: Integrating Embeddings from Multiple Protein Language Models to Improve Protein O-GlcNAc Site Prediction
pmc-10650050.creator: Suresh Pokharel, Pawel Pratyush, Hamid D Ismail, Junfeng Ma, Dukka B KC, Kazunori Hamamura
pmc-10650050.description: O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine (O-GlcNAc) is a distinct monosaccharide modification of serine (S) or threonine (T) residues of nucleocytoplasmic and mitochondrial proteins. O-GlcNAc modification (i.e., O-GlcNAcylation) is involved in the regulation of diverse cellular processes, including transcription, epigenetic modifications, and cell signaling.

pmc-11456583.title: A microglial compliment: controlling neuronal function from within
pmc-11456583.creator: Dilara Hasavci, Thomas Blank
pmc-11456583.description: significant implications for understanding age-related changes in brain function and potentially neurodegenerative diseases.1 Microglia are responsible for surveilling the central nervous system, responding to changes and injuries, phagocytosing cellular debris and protein aggregates, pruning synapses during development, releasing factors that influence neural function, and mediating immune responses in the brain2 (Fig. 1).

pmc-11598007.title: Quantum Privacy-Preserving Range Query Protocol for Encrypted Data in IoT Environments
pmc-11598007.creator: Chong-Qiang Ye, Jian Li, Xiao-Yu Chen
pmc-11598007.description: With the rapid development of IoT technology, securely querying sensitive data collected by devices within a specific range has become a focal concern for users. This paper proposes a privacy-preserving range query scheme based on quantum encryption, along with circuit simulations and performance analysis.

pmc-11625154.title: Enhanced osteogenic potential of spider silk fibroin-based composite scaffolds incorporating carboxymethyl cellulose for bone tissue engineering
pmc-11625154.creator: Woong Jin Lee, Kyoungjoo Cho, Dayoon Lee, Seungmin Lee, Hyojae Jeon, Aaron Youngjae Kim, Gyung Whan Kim
pmc-11625154.description: Highlights•The CMC/spidroin scaffold exhibited high cell viability with no indications of any cytotoxicity towards BMSCs.•The addition of CMC to spidroin-only scaffold creates ideal conditions for regeneration of bone structures.•The CMC/spidroin scaffold boosted osteogenic differentiation. Introduction Scaffolds are a crucial component in tissue engineering, providing a supportive structure for cell growth and tissue regeneration.

pmc-12415268.title: Development of a Plant‐Based Chocolate Spread With Enhanced Vitamin D3 Bioavailability and Balanced Omega Fatty Acids
pmc-12415268.creator: Dina E. H. Azab, Ebtehal A. Altamim, Tarek N. Soliman, Sahar A. Nasser, Hamdy A. Zahran
pmc-12415268.description: This study developed a vegan chocolate spread using spray‐dried plant‐based milk powders (soy, lentil, and rice), fortified with nano‐liposomal vitamin D3 and an oleogel‐balanced omega fatty acid to enhance nutritional quality. The plant‐based milk powders exhibited high protein (up to 26.8% in soy), fiber, and micronutrients.

pmc-12465201.title: Base curves of bandage contact lenses and their effects on post Trans-PRK vision and pain: the study protocol for a randomized clinical trial
pmc-12465201.creator: Gengmin Tong, Yuanhui Jin, Hangshuai Zhou, Yanhua Jin
pmc-12465201.description: BackgroundTransepithelial photorefractive keratectomy (Trans-PRK) is an effective and safe laser surgery for myopia. Following this procedure, a bandage contact lens is used to promote epithelial healing, reduce postoperative pain, and improve visual recovery. The base curve of these lenses may affect vision post-surgery, particularly in patients with steep corneas and high myopia.

pmc-12640202.title: Closer friends have more similar actigraphy-estimated sleep patterns
pmc-12640202.creator: Venetia Jing Tong Kok, Clin K Y Lai, Annadata V Rukmini, Hana Yabuki, Joshua J Gooley
pmc-12640202.description: Study ObjectivesIndividuals in close relationships often show similarities in health lifestyle behaviors. Here, we tested associations between friendship closeness and sleep patterns in university students. We hypothesized that daily actigraphy-estimated sleep timing and duration would be more similar in closer friendships with evidence of positive covariation.

pmc-13469828.title: Experiences of Accessing Physical Rehabilitation Services and Assistive Products Among Orthosis and Wheelchair Users: Qualitative Study
pmc-13469828.creator: Charlotte Spurway, Andrew Power, Maggie Donovan-Hall, Andrew Amos Channon, Sarah Munce, Anonymous, Sejun Oh

pmc-13609532.title: Clinical Outcomes and Factors Associated with Response to Fluoroscopy-Guided Cervical Medial Branch Pulsed Radiofrequency in Chronic Cervical Facet Joint Pain: A Retrospective Cohort Study
pmc-13609532.creator: Nevcihan Şahutoğlu Bal, Şükriye Dadalı, Ali Çoştu, Gülçin Babaoğlu, Ülkü Sabuncu, Emel Başar, Erkan Yavuz Akçaboy
pmc-13609532.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background and Objectives: Pulsed radiofrequency (PRF) of the cervical medial branches is a non-destructive neuromodulatory option for chronic cervical facet joint pain, yet evidence regarding the durability of clinical response and factors associated with sustained benefit remains limited. This study aimed to characterize the 6-month trajectory of pain and disability after fluoroscopy-guided cervical medial branch PRF and to explore baseline factors associated with meaningful pain relief (MPR).
